transcript: I have to talk about how much I love the non proposal scene in volume 2 of Stranger Things, which is apparently a hot take, so spoilers ahead for volume 2 of season 5 if you haven't watched it yet. But I just think that this is such a beautiful breakup scene. And yes, it's a breakup scene. I don't know why that's under debate, but I think one of my biggest issues with season 5 as a whole is the lack of stakes in the show. That it feels like people are surviving things that they shouldn't be surviving, that the show has all of a sudden become afraid of killing off characters when it did not at all have that issue in previous seasons. But while this scene doesn't kill off either Nancy or Jonathan, despite the fact that they are on the brink of death, and the stakes are so incredibly high, it does take the scene to sink both of Nancy's ships. And I just think that's brilliant, because in this entire series, Nancy has always been attached to one of these men in the show, whether it's Steve or Jonathan. And so to take this scene to really just have her admit, hey, I, I, I don't, I, I love Steve, but I don't see myself with him. Like, we aren't compatible. And also, I love you, but I'm okay with this relationship ending, too. Like that. Brilliant. And the fact that Jonathan also is Admitting, like, you know, I was gonna propose to you, and I don't. I don't think that's the right move. Like, we're not good together. We've trauma bonded and that's about it. Like, that's brilliant. So often in these types of media, especially the media from the 80s, that Stranger Things takes a lot of influence from the trope that Nancy fits into as a character. Often it is attached to a guy of some sort. And so the fact that she is choosing and realises that she's not compatible with either of the men in her life is refreshing to see, especially knowing her mother and how her mother fit into that same trope and where her mother ended up in life in an incredibly unhappy marriage. So while I wish stranger things would shy away from killing off characters in its final season, I'm really glad that they killed off these relationships. I'm really, really happy about it. And there's something so beautiful about two characters coming to the conclusion that even though they love each other and respect each other, that they know that they're not right for each other. And we rarely see that in this type of media that's geared towards, like, teenagers. And so it's just beautiful to see that they're okay splitting up, even on the brink of death. And to come to that realisation in your final moments of your life, that's something that we never get to see. Usually it's a Profession of love, not a profession of. I love you, but we're not right for each other. And that's why I think so many people are confused by this scene. But it's very clear from the context clues of the non proposal of them leaving the ring in the room that this isn't. This isn't an actual proposal. This is in fact a breakup. And a beautiful one at that.
